entities.name: Baitul Aman Mosque
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Baitul Aman Mosque (House of Peace) in Barisal, Bangladesh, is one of the most architecturally distinctive mosques in Bangladesh — known for its extraordinary dome-heavy design featuring numerous small domes surrounding a central large dome, creating a silhouette unlike any other mosque in the country. Built in the early 21st century with local and diaspora funding, the mosque reflects Bangladesh's thriving tradition of elaborate mosque construction that has accelerated since independence (1971), particularly in smaller cities and towns.

Bangladesh is the world's third-largest Muslim-majority country with approximately 150 million Muslims (roughly 90% of the population), and mosque construction has been a prominent form of community investment and piety. The post-independence period has seen extraordinary mosque-building across Bangladesh, from simple rural mosques to elaborate urban structures. Baitul Aman's multi-dome design draws on the Mughal mosque tradition (notably the famous Sixty Dome Mosque at Bagerhat, a UNESCO World Heritage Site) while adapting it to modern construction techniques and materials.

Barisal — the main city of Bangladesh's Barisal Division — is a river delta city surrounded by waterways, and the Baitul Aman Mosque serves as one of the region's major religious landmarks and a gathering point for the substantial Muslim community of southern Bangladesh. The mosque exemplifies how Bangladeshi Islamic architecture has created a distinct regional tradition combining historical Mughal and Indian Islamic influences with modernist construction.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Baitul Aman Mosque — a distinctive multi-dome regional landmark in Bangladesh combining Mughal architectural heritage with modern construction, representing post-independence Bangladeshi mosque-building culture and diaspora investment in homeland religious infrastructure — reflects the vitality of Islamic architectural tradition in South Asia.
